earnings_release.text: EX-99.1 2 uri-9302026xex991.htm EX-99.1 Document Exhibit 99.1 United Rentals, Inc. 100 First Stamford Place, Suite 700 Stamford, CT 06902 Telephone: 203 622 3131 unitedrentals.com United Rentals Announces Record Third Quarter Results and Raises Full-Year 2026 Guidance STAMFORD, Conn. – October 21, 2026 – United Rentals, Inc. (NYSE: URI) today announced record financial results for the third quarter of 2026, and raised its 2026 full-year guidance. Third Quarter 2026 Highlights • Total revenue of $4.893 billion, including rental revenue 1 of $4.316 billion. • Net income of $920 million, at a margin 2 of 18.8%. GAAP diluted earnings per share (“EPS”) of $14.77, and adjusted EPS 3 of $15.55. • Adjusted EBITDA 3 of $2.331 billion, at a margin 2 of 47.6%. • Year-over-year, fleet productivity 4 increased 6.5%. • Year-to-date net cash provided by operating activities of $4.934 billion; free cash flow 3 of $1.421 billion, including gross payments for purchases of rental equipment of $4.339 billion. • Year-to-date gross rental capital expenditures of $4.746 billion. • Returned $1.496 billion to shareholders year-to-date, comprised of $1.125 billion via share repurchases and $371 million via dividends paid. • Net leverage ratio 5 of 1.8x, with total liquidity 5 of $2.615 billion, at September 30, 2026. CEO Comment Matthew Flannery, chief executive officer of United Rentals, said, “I’m very pleased with our third-quarter results, which are a testament to our strategy, our team’s dedication to our customers, and the unmatched breadth and scale of our premier offering. We continued to lean into growth across both our general rentals and specialty businesses with the momentum from the first half of the year carrying through the quarter.” Flannery continued, “As we look ahead, we believe we are uniquely positioned to outperform the industry through our broad footprint, unmatched one-stop-shop offering, exceptional levels of service, leading technology and unwavering commitment to safety. Our raised guidance reflects this, and is supported by our customers’ confidence, their backlogs, and the momentum we see across large projects. I am very proud of the company we continue to build, underpinned by a well-proven strategy of supporting our customers while also driving profitable growth and strong through-cycle free cash flow generation. Combined with prudent capital allocation, this will continue to deliver compelling long-term value for our shareholders.” _______________ 1. Rental revenue includes owned equipment rental revenue, re-rent revenue and ancillary revenue. 2. Net income margin and adjusted EBITDA margin represent net income or adjusted EBITDA divided by total revenue. 3. Adjusted EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization), adjusted EPS (earnings per share) and free cash flow are non-GAAP financial measures as defined in the tables below. See the tables below for reconciliations to the most comparable GAAP measures. 4. Fleet productivity reflects the combined impact of changes in rental rates, time utilization and mix on owned equipment rental revenue. 5. The net leverage ratio reflects net debt (total debt less cash and cash equivalents) divided by adjusted EBITDA for the trailing 12 months. Total liquidity reflects cash and cash equivalents plus availability under the asset-based revolving credit facility (“ABL facility”) and the accounts receivable securitization facility. 2026 Outlook The company has raised its 2026 outlook, as reflected below. Current Outlook Prior Outlook Total revenue $18.0 billion to $18.2 billion $17.5 billion to $17.8 billion Adjusted EBITDA 6 $8.3 billion to $8.4 billion $7.975 billion to $8.125 billion Net rental capital expenditures after gross purchases $3.75 billion to $4.05 billion, after gross purchases of $5.2 billion to $5.5 billion $3.4 billion to $3.8 billion, after gross purchases of $4.85 billion to $5.25 billion Net cash provided by operating activities $6.25 billion to $6.85 billion $5.85 billion to $6.65 billion Free cash flow excluding restructuring related payments 7 $2.15 billion to $2.45 billion $2.15 billion to $2.45 billion Summary of Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results • Rental revenue increased 17.8% year-over-year, to a quarterly record of $4.316 billion, primarily due to a 7.9% increase in average original equipment at cost (“OEC”), strong demand as reflected in a 6.5% increase in fleet productivity, and a 4.9% contribution from ancillary and re-rent revenue. • Used equipment sales in the quarter increased 4.5% year-over-year. Used equipment sales generated $348 million of proceeds at a GAAP gross margin of 44.8% and an adjusted gross margin 8 of 46.3%, compared to a GAAP gross margin of 44.1% and an adjusted gross margin of 45.9% for the same period last year. The company realized a 51.4% OEC recovery rate on the fleet sold in the third quarter of 2026. • Net income for the quarter increased 31.2% year-over-year to a third quarter record of $920 million, while net income margin increased 220 basis points to 18.8%, primarily due to increased rental gross margin. The increase in rental gross margin primarily reflected, for both the general rentals and specialty rentals segments, the impact of efficiencies in depreciation, labor and benefits, repairs and maintenance, and delivery expenses, partially offset by the impact of changes in revenue mix driven by growth in lower-margin ancillary and re-rent revenues. • Adjusted EBITDA for the quarter increased 19.8% year-over-year to a quarterly record of $2.331 billion, while adjusted EBITDA margin increased 160 basis points to 47.6%, primarily reflecting increased rental gross margin (excluding depreciation and stock compensation expense), a reduction in selling, general and administrative ("SG&A") expenses as a percentage of revenue, and an increase in the proportion of revenue from equipment rentals. The increase in rental gross margin is discussed above (the discussion above includes depreciation, while, on the adjusted EBITDA basis, rental gross margin excludes depreciation). • General rentals segment rental revenue increased 8.8% year-over-year to a quarterly record of $2.612 billion, while rental gross margin increased by 170 basis points year-over-year to 38.4%, primarily due to the drivers discussed above. • Specialty rentals segment rental revenue increased 34.7% year-over-year to a quarterly record of $1.704 billion. Rental gross margin increased by 250 basis points year-over-year to 47.6%, primarily due to the drivers discussed above. _______________ 6. Information reconciling forward-looking adjusted EBITDA to the comparable GAAP financial measures is unavailable to the company without unreasonable effort, as discussed below. 7. Free cash flow excludes restructuring related payments, which cannot be reasonably predicted for the 2026 outlook. Restructuring related payments were $27 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026. 8. Used equipment sales adjusted gross margin is a non-GAAP financial measure that excludes the impact ($5 million and $6 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively) of the fair value mark-up of fleet acquired in certain major acquisitions that was subsequently sold. This adjustment is explained further in the tables below, and represents the only difference between the GAAP gross margin and the adjusted gross margin. 2 • Cash flow from operating activities increased 25.4% to $4.934 billion, and free cash flow, including restructuring related payments, increased 19.2% to $1.421 billion, year-over-year, for the first nine months of 2026. • Capital management. The company’s net leverage ratio was 1.8x at September 30, 2026, as compared to 1.9x at December 31, 2025. During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the company completed its prior $2.0 billion share repurchase 9 program, and commenced its new $5.0 billion share repurchase program. During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the company repurchased $1.125 billion of common stock under these programs, and paid dividends totaling $371 million. The company expects to complete $1.5 billion of share repurchases in 2026. Additionally, the company’s Board of Directors has declared a quarterly dividend of $1.97 per share, payable on November 25, 2026 to stockholders of record on November 11, 2026. • Total liquidity was $2.615 billion as of September 30, 2026, including $153 million of cash and cash equivalents. • Return on invested capital (ROIC) 10 was 12.3% for the 12 months ended September 30, 2026. Conference Call United Rentals will hold a conference call tomorrow, Thursday, October 22, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time. The conference call number is 800-791-4799 (international: 785-424-1631). The replay number for the call is 402-220-0687. The passcode for both the conference call and the replay is 31810. The conference call will also be available live by audio webcast at unitedrentals.com, where it will be archived until the next earnings call. _______________ 9. All references to share repurchases above do not include the excise tax, which totaled $10 million year-to-date through September 30, 2026. 10. The company’s ROIC metric uses after-tax operating income for the trailing 12 months divided by average stockholders’ equity, debt and deferred taxes, net of average cash. To mitigate the volatility related to fluctuations in the company’s tax rate from period to period, the U.S. federal corporate statutory tax rate of 21% was used to calculate after-tax operating income. 3 Non-GAAP Financial Measures Free cash flow, earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA), adjusted EBITDA, adjusted earnings per share (adjusted EPS) and used equipment sales adjusted gross margin are non-GAAP financial measures as defined under the rules of the SEC. Free cash flow represents net cash provided by operating activities less payments for purchases of, and plus proceeds from, equipment and intangible assets. The equipment and intangible asset items are included in cash flows from investing activities. EBITDA represents the sum of net income, provision for income taxes, interest expense, net, depreciation of rental equipment and non-rental depreciation and amortization. Adjusted EBITDA represents EBITDA plus the sum of the restructuring charges, stock compensation expense, net, and the impact of the fair value mark-up of acquired fleet. Adjusted EPS represents EPS plus the sum of the restructuring charges, the impact on depreciation related to acquired fleet and property and equipment, the impact of the fair value mark-up of acquired fleet, merger related intangible asset amortization, asset impairment charge and debt related losses. Used equipment sales adjusted gross margin excludes the impact of the fair value mark-up of fleet acquired in certain major acquisitions that was subsequently sold (this adjustment is explained further in the adjusted EPS and EBITDA/adjusted EBITDA tables below). The company believes that: (i) free cash flow provides useful additional information concerning cash flow available to meet future debt service obligations and working capital requirements; (ii) EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA provide useful information about operating performance and period-over-period growth, and help investors gain an understanding of the factors and trends affecting our ongoing cash earnings, from which capital investments are made and debt is serviced; (iii) adjusted EPS provides useful information concerning future profitability; and (iv) used equipment sales adjusted gross margin provides information that is useful for evaluating the profitability of used equipment sales without regard to potential distortions. reference.summary: United Rentals, Inc., through its subsidiaries, operates as an equipment rental company in the United States, Canada, Europe, Australia, and New Zealand. It operates through two segments, General Rentals and Specialty. The General Rentals segment rents general construction and industrial equipment, such as backhoes, skid-steer loaders, forklifts, earthmoving equipment, and material handling equipment; aerial work platforms, including boom and scissor lifts; and general tools and light equipment comprising pressure washers, water pumps, and power tools for construction and industrial companies, manufacturers, utilities, municipalities, homeowners, and government entities.
